name: Romania

fees.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - adult
fees.notes: Romania applies the common EU/Schengen-associated short-stay visa fee (raised to EUR 90 in June 2024, confirmed current on EU Commission migration/home-affairs page). Romania is an EU member applying the common visa policy for non-Schengen-area short stays; national embassies issue the visa under this standard fee schedule. Could not reach mae.ro (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) directly - site returned a bot-verification/503 response during this check, so this figure is corroborated via the EU Commission official source and cross-checked against secondary aggregator sites rather than a direct MFA fee-schedule page.

fees.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - child aged 6-12
fees.notes: Reduced fee per common EU rules; children under 6 typically exempt.

fees.name: Airport/Transit Visa (Type A/B)
fees.notes: Secondary sources report transit visa fees are typically the same as the short-stay visa fee, but this was not confirmed on an official government page; amount withheld pending direct MFA verification.

fees.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - business purpose
fees.applies: adults from visa-required nationalities, business purpose
fees.notes: Business short-stay visas fall under the same Type C fee schedule as tourist visas.

reciprocity_variations.note: EU suspended the EU-Russia visa facilitation agreement in 2022; Russian nationals may face higher fees and no facilitation benefits, but an exact current figure was not confirmed on an official Romanian source during this check.

vfs.note: VFS Global operates Romania visa application centres in several countries including India. Published/aggregator estimates place the India service fee around INR 1,500-2,500 per applicant in addition to the consular visa fee, but this was not verified on VFS Global's own fee page during this check (only secondary aggregator sources were accessible) - treat as indicative, not authoritative.

free_visa_notes: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens and holders of certain valid Schengen visas do not need a separate Romanian visa for short stays. Romania is progressively integrating into the Schengen area (air/sea borders from 2024, land borders joining in 2025-2026); short-stay visa policy already follows the common Schengen fee schedule for non-exempt nationalities.
